shortDescription: Italy's service sector grew in August at its fastest rate in almost 3-1/2 years, a survey showed on Thursday, in a positive sign for the euro zone's third-largest economy.

children: Italy's service sector grew in August at its fastest rate in almost 3-1/2 years, a survey showed on Thursday, in a positive sign for the euro zone's third-largest economy.
S&P Global's Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) for the Italian service sector jumped to 55.2 from July's 52.5, moving further above the 50 threshold that separates growth from contraction.
A Reuters survey of 12 analysts had pointed to a reading of 54.0.
"Strong growth in activity and new business puts the sector on track to see its best quarter of the year so far," said S&P Global economist Eleanor Dennison.
The survey's "new business" indicator climbed to 55.6 from 53.9, to post the highest reading since March 2024.
Its measure of input cost inflation rose slightly to 61.5 from 61.2, while the indicator of prices charged fell to 52.5 from 53.3, registering the lowest level in eight months.
The Italian economy has held up better than many analysts expected in the first half of this year, with gross domestic product rising by 0.3% in the first quarter and 0.2% in the second.
Giorgia Meloni's government in April forecast full-year 2026 growth of 0.6%.
S&P Global's sister survey for Italy's smaller manufacturing sector, released on Tuesday, showed contraction in August for the first time in seven months.
However, the composite PMI, combining manufacturing and services, rose to 53.6 in August from 52.5, the fifth straight month of expansion and the highest reading since November last year.
